messages:
alexa: Heads-up — I'm seeing intermittent parse errors when client is under burst load. partial JSON chunks arriving, then parser throws mid-object. reproducer attached in gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/sse-burst-repro

sam: ah, saw that earlier — is this the corking behavior on iOS client? when connection w/ gzip flushes small chunks?

alexa: yep looks similar. but repro is Node native client too. seems when small chunks contain half a unicode code point + partial json, our incremental decoder returns error instead of waiting for more.

kai: can we treat it as benign and buffer until we get a full object? what's the current backpressure model in the SDK?

maria: SDK uses a non-blocking readable stream + JSON incremental parser. we try to emit partial objects, but we rely on the stream to coalesce. under heavy load the OS socket gives tiny slices (Nagle off) so parser sees truncated utf8.

ben: suggestion: on JSON decode error, check if last byte is an incomplete UTF-8 sequence and then backoff + request more data for up to X ms before failing. basic pseudocode:```js
try { parse(chunk) } catch(e) { if (looksLikeTruncatedUtf8(chunk)) { await stream.waitForMore(50) ; continue } else throw e }```

sam: agreed. also we should gate retries so we don't block eventloop for long — maybe exponential backoff with capped ms. and metric the number of buffered-retries so infra can see spikes.

alexa: good call. two pragmatic Qs: 1) what default max wait is safe? 2) do we want bail if overall request latency > route SLO?

maria: I'd default to 30ms and cap at 200ms total per request. if request crosses SLO (configurable per route) we stop buffering and fall back to a non-streaming call or smaller model.

kai: for Dedicated customers we can expose config, for hosted keep defaults. also log an event with flags: truncated_utf8_retry, bytes_buffered, total_wait_ms.

infra-bot: deploy scheduled: sse-parser-softfix -> staging in 30m, canary 5% for 1h.

ben: small nit: add an opt-in env var RAW_PARSE_STRICT=true for debugging in dev so we can fail-fast when teams want to see errors rather than silent buffering.

alexa: I'll open a PR with parser change + metrics + env var. assigning to @sam for review, @maria for SDK semantics check.

sam: lgtm. quick code comment: ensure we don't reallocate huge buffers — use a ring buffer or slice view.

maria: will review SDK surface. if we add fallback to non-streaming, document in changelog.

alexa: thanks — will ping here when PR is up. :thumbsup:
